Milestone 2 Report

§1 Project definition & development

This project re-engineers a Milestone 1 (M1) notebook into a documented, repeatable data-handling and infrastructure pipeline for healthcare-fraud detection. The central goal of Milestone 2 is not a model — it is to demonstrate understanding of the data and to move it through a repeatable pipeline, earning every design decision with evidence rather than taking it on faith.

The pipeline implements the bronze / silver / gold medallion architecture. Raw data is held untouched as the source of truth (bronze); it is cleaned, typed, validated and imputed into a trusted intermediate (silver); and it is finally transformed into a model-ready feature matrix (gold) that can feed a classifier in a later milestone. Every transition is checked, and every tier carries a chained manifest so the provenance of the final feature set is provable end-to-end.

Success is defined as: a leakage-free, model-ready feature set in cloud storage whose preparation is reproducible, whose decisions are each evidenced by analysis, and whose provenance can be reconciled at every step — not a tuned model.

The work extends M1 rather than duplicating it. Where M1 justified decisions narratively, M2 re-earns them with numbers (decision-log D1–D18); where M1 treated cleaning and feature engineering as one flow, M2 makes the three tiers explicit; and where M1 had documented pipeline lapses — an amount transform that was claimed but not implemented (D13), a velocity threshold that contradicted its own headline (D14) — M2 fixes them and records why.

Scope: no final predictive model and no test-set evaluation are produced in this milestone; the finish line is the model-ready gold tier. A model plan is given (Milestone 3, §8) but is deliberately out of scope here, consistent with the rubric.

§2 Data provenance, governance & ethics

2.1 Source, licence & acquisition

The dataset is the Healthcare Fraud Detection Dataset, published on Kaggle by Nudrat Abbas (kaggle.com/datasets/nudratabbas/healthcare-fraud-detection-dataset). It is distributed under the CC0 public-domain licence, which permits redistribution and reuse without restriction. Because the data is fully synthetic medical-billing records — engineered with log-normal distributions to mimic real-world claim behaviour and billing anomalies rather than derived from any individuals — no personally identifiable information (PII) is present, and so the usual privacy-protection obligations do not arise here (we state this explicitly rather than imply it).

Acquisition is version-pinned and reproducible. The dataset is fetched via kagglehub.dataset_download(version=1) exactly once, at the acquisition stage of the pipeline, and ingested into the bronze tier; the fetch is a bootstrap step, after which the pipeline reads from cloud storage, never from Kaggle. The bronze object's file-level sha256 (5031a157…) was verified byte-identical to the bundled local copy, so the exact ingested bytes are pinned and auditable.

2.2 Provenance & the raw layer (bronze → silver → gold)

The pipeline implements the bronze / silver / gold medallion model from the Week-6 material, which centres on the invariant "keep the raw layer untouched." Each tier materialises (D17/D18) and carries a manifest.json — sha256 digest, row/column shape and source — that chains it to the tier it was produced from:

  • Bronze — the raw, unmodified source of truth (write-once; never altered in place).
  • Silver — cleaned, typed, validated and imputed, written at close-of-silver (after cast → validate → impute waves, D1/D2/D17), with its manifest chained to bronze.
  • Gold — the model-ready feature matrix (19 pre-encoding features + Is_Fraud + split; D16), with its manifest carrying source_silver, split counts and fraud rate, chained to silver.

This chained manifest is a reconciliation proof: at every transition, the reading stage verifies the source tier's sha256 + shape before ingesting (schema-contract assert at silver, integrity gate at gold), so provenance is enforced, not asserted. The stored gold object is verified reproducible — cold re-runs produce a byte-identical artifact (gold sha256 4541d519…).

Storage governance. Raw and derived tiers live in a Google Cloud Storage bucket (milestone_two), partitioned by date ({date}/bronze|silver|gold/), with object versioning enabled. We note one tension honestly: the bucket's lifecycle policy deletes non-current object versions after 7 days. This does not violate the immutability invariant — the current bronze object is never overwritten in place (write-once), and its content is byte-pinned by the manifest sha256 — but it does mean we do not retain indefinite full version history; only the authoritative current object and its digest are preserved. We deliberately state this bound: immutability of the raw layer holds (current bronze is write-once and byte-pinned); unbounded version-history retention does not (bounded by the lifecycle). The Week-6 frame — "a good pipeline keeps the raw layer untouched" — is what we mean by "immutable," and that is exactly what is preserved.

2.3 Fairness, bias & governance of model output

Protected characteristics are excluded by design. Patient_Age and Patient_Gender are deliberately excluded at gold (D12). This is not a capability trade-off: the EDA evidence (EV5) shows these fields carry no predictive signal — gender is balanced at ~8.3% fraud for each value (Cramér's V 0.0047) and age shows no meaningful association (point-biserial r = −0.017) — so excluding them costs ~nothing while removing protected attributes from the feature set.

Target leakage is guarded as an ethical-cum-rigour matter. Claim_Status (a downstream, post-decision adjudication outcome available after the point of prediction) is excluded (D10) because it near-encodes the target (fraud 2.2% in Approved vs 22.7% / 23.1% in Pending / Rejected — EV3). Using it would both leak the target and bake the adjudication outcome the model is meant to help evaluate back into the model. We document rather than silently drop (D10).

Governance of outputs. The purpose of this pipeline is to produce model-ready features for investigation, not to make automated punitive decisions. Consequently, any model downstream of this pipeline is intended to flag a claim for human review / investigation — never to automatically deny payment or impose a decision (D12 governance). The velocity ("fast") feature is likewise a model-fed input, not a hard denial rule (D14): because it overlaps ~18% of legitimate claims, it must never be used as a standalone rejection rule. This keeps the human-in-the-loop as the decision-maker and the model as a triage aid.

2.4 Limitations (honest, not papered over)

  • Synthetic-data generalisation. Because the source is fully synthetic, a model trained on it may not generalise to real-world billing fraud. We own this explicitly: the milestone's value is a defensible, reproducible data-handling pipeline built on a suitably realistic synthetic dataset; any real deployment must (re)validate against genuine claim data before use.
  • Class imbalance. The target is unbalanced (8.29% fraudulent); the 8 CV fold structure over train is verified class-balanced in the evidence pass (EV9) — guaranteeing the leak-free denominator for Milestone-3 model cross-validation — but no model is trained or cross-validated in this milestone (per scope, §1); downstream modelling of the imbalance is Milestone-3 work.
  • Scope. No final predictive model under test-set-CV is built in this milestone (the finish line is the model-ready gold tier); the impact of transforms (e.g. log1p, D13) is documented as distributional hygiene rather than an accuracy claim.

§3 Data description

Unit of analysis. Each row is one healthcare claim. The dataset contains 10,000 rows × 20 columns.

Target. Is_Fraud is the binary target. The class balance is 8.29% fraudulent (829 of 10,000), which is the baseline any downstream model must beat.

Schema by role. Columns split into clear roles (full details in data/data_card.md §Schema):

Role Columns Handling
Identifiers Claim_ID not features (D11)
Patient / protected Patient_Age, Patient_Gender excluded at gold (D12, fairness — EV5)
Clinical / payer / visit categoricals Provider_Specialty, Diagnosis_Code, Procedure_Code, Patient_State, Insurance_Type, Visit_Type imputed (D2) → target-encoded at gold (D4)
Financial Claim_Amount, Approved_Amount log1p + standardised at gold (D13)
Temporal Claim_Submission_Date date dropped; Submission_Month + weekend kept (D3)
Volume / stay / history Prior_Visits_12m, Length_of_Stay, Days_Between_Service_and_Claim velocity profiled (D7/D14)
Settlement outcome Claim_Status excluded (D10, leakage — EV3)
Claim-internal Provider_ID not a feature

Time range. Claims span 2021-01-06 → 2025-01-26 (49 months) with no gaps requiring handling.

Missingness. Three fields each have 350 missing values before imputation: Insurance_Type, Provider_Specialty, Prior_Visits_12m. The missingness analysis (EV1, §4) shows the pattern is uninformative with respect to fraud, so simple imputation is chosen (D1/D2). Zero duplicate rows and zero duplicate Claim_IDs (D11) — no deduplication step is required, and none is silently assumed.

Known limitation. The data is synthetic; this is stated in §2.4 and not treated as real-world evidence.

§4 Exploratory data analysis (purposeful, decision-driving)

The EDA below is interpretive: each finding is stated, then tied to the specific decision it earns (D#). This is the heart of the milestone — the EDA drives data-quality, preprocessing, splitting and pipeline decisions, rather than being a gallery of charts.

4.1 Missingness is non-informative → impute simply (D1, D2)

Three columns (Insurance_Type, Provider_Specialty, Prior_Visits_12m) each carry 350 nulls. We asked why they are missing before choosing how to handle them (EV1): the fraud rate among rows with a missing value is statistically flat against the baseline — insurance-missing 7.1% vs 8.3% present, specialty-missing 8.6%, prior-visits-missing 8.3%. The co-missing pattern also separates cleanly (326 / 323 / 325 rows miss a single field; only 2 rows miss all three; joint cells of overlap are tiny, n ≤ 13). Plainly, missingness does not encode class. Decision: impute Prior_Visits_12m → 0 and the two categoricals → a neutral "Unknown" token (D1/D2). The noisy joint cells (n ≤ 13) argued against engineering missing-indicator features — there is no signal to capture, and the added dimensions buy nothing.

Missingness mechanism. The flat class-conditional rates rule out missingness being driven by the fraud status of the unobserved value — target-driven MNAR is therefore implausible. From the observed data alone we cannot definitively separate MCAR from MAR, and a general MNAR (correlation with the missing value itself) cannot be excluded without external information or sensitivity analysis; we treat the mechanism as non-informative (consistent with MCAR/MAR) rather than assert a proven one.

4.2 The timeline trap → velocity profiling with a ≤6-day rule (D7, D14)

The single clearest signal in the data is speed (EV2): legitimate claims take a mean of 15.45 days (median 15, range 2–29) between service and submission, while fraudulent claims take a mean of 2.97 days (median 3, range 0–6) — fraud is both much faster and extremely reliably fast: 100% of fraudulent claims are submitted within 6 days. This justifies transforming the raw day-count into a velocity profile (D7) rather than using it raw. Decision on the threshold (D14): the "fast" flag is set at ≤ 6 days, which captures 100% of fraud (a ≤5-day rule would have caught only 87.2% and contradicted the evidence — this reconciles a reported-6-days/coded-5-days mismatch inherited from M1). Critically, ~18% of legitimate claims are also fast, so the feature is a model-fed input, not a standalone denial rule (§2.3).

4.3 Leakage hazard + data-quality baseline (D10, D11)

Claim_Status — a downstream adjudication outcome decided after the point of prediction — near-encodes the target (EV3): fraud is 2.2% among Approved claims but 22.7% / 23.1% among Pending / Rejected. Feeding it in would leak the target and bake the very decision the model should evaluate back into the model. Decision: exclude Claim_Status from all features, and document the exclusion rather than drop it silently (D10). Separately, a quality audit found 0 duplicate rows and 0 duplicate Claim_IDs — so no deduplication step is warranted, and we record that rather than run a needless one (D11).

4.4 Protected characteristics carry no signal → exclude (D12, fairness)

Patient_Age and Patient_Gender were present in M1 but dropped without justification. We measured their association with the target before deciding (EV5): gender is balanced at ~8.3% fraud for each value (Cramér's V 0.0047) and age shows a negligible association (point-biserial r = −0.017). There is no predictive signal to lose. Decision: exclude both at gold — a fairness-by-design choice that costs nothing while removing protected attributes from the feature set (§2.3).

4.5 Financial fields are heavily skewed → log-then-standardise (D13)

Claim_Amount and Approved_Amount are strongly right-skewed (skew 2.4 and 2.1; legitimate median $385 vs a fraudulent tail to $6,590.70). Skew of this size distorts distance-based preprocessing (EV4). M1 claimed a log-transform in its README but actually ran a standard scaler on raw values — a documented drift we correct. Decision: apply np.log1p then StandardScaler at gold (D13); this collapses skew to 0.102 and 0.055 (EV6). We state the honest caveat: on tree-based models this is pipeline-correctness and distributional hygiene, not an accuracy win.

4.6 Cardinality is low everywhere → encode by signal, not to avoid explosion (D4)

A direct cardinality count shows every categorical field is low-cardinality — Diagnosis_Code 10, Procedure_Code 9, Provider_Specialty 6, Patient_State 8, Insurance_Type 4, Visit_Type 3 — max 10 (EV9). This reframes the reason for target encoding: M1's framing (avoid one-hot "dimension explosion") does not hold on this data, since one-hotting all six would add only ~40 columns (trivial at 10k rows). Decision: the pipeline uses smooth target encoding (TargetEncoder(smooth=10)) for a different and defensible reason — capturing per-category fraud signal with smoothing regularisation (D4, reframed). No dimension-explosion justification is claimed.

Forward-compatibility note. The current data is low-cardinality (max 10), so the TargetEncoder choice here is earned by fraud-signal capture with smoothing regularisation, not by dimension-explosion. That said, real-world medical code taxonomies (ICD-10 ≈ 70k codes, CPT ≈ 10k) are far larger than this synthetic dataset's few dozen values, and a future or more realistic version could expand cardinality substantially. Two design properties make the pipeline robust to that: (1) target encoding remains cheap and leak-free under high cardinality, where one-hot would grow quadratically-brittle storage; and (2) because encoding is fit-per-fold inside the training pipeline (D16), not written into gold, the encoding strategy itself can be swapped (e.g. for a learned embedding) without re-cutting the stored feature matrix.

4.7 Splits and folds are class-balanced → stratified split and leak-free CV stand (D6, D8)

The 80/10/10 stratified split (8000 / 1000 / 1000 rows) preserves the ~8.3% fraud rate across all three partitions (EV9): 0.0829 / 0.0830 / 0.0830. Each of the 8 cross-validation folds also stays within the ~8.3% band. Decision: the 8-fold CV fold structure over train is verified class-balanced in the evidence pass (EV9) — guaranteeing the leak-free denominator for Milestone-3 model cross-validation — but no model is trained or cross-validated in this milestone (per scope, §1); the stratified split and fold balance stand on the numbers (D6/D8). Splitting and preprocessing are ordered leak-free: all scaling/encoding is fit per-fold inside the training loop and never on the full dataset (D8/D16).

4.8 No systematic seasonality → date kept as month + weekend only (D3)

Fraud over the 49-month window (2021-01 → 2025-01) shows no systematic calendar season — month-level rates oscillate between about 0.046 and 0.121 with no repeatable pattern (EV9). Decision: the raw submission date is dropped after deriving Submission_Month and a weekend indicator (D3); no calendar-based feature engineering is warranted.

4.9 Result: a clean, balanced, model-ready gold matrix

The cumulative effect of §4.1–4.8 is a gold tier of 10,000 rows × 21 columns = 19 pre-encoding features + Is_Fraud + split, with 0 nulls, fraud balanced to 0.0829 overall, and any drop of a column (dates, protected attributes, identifiers, Claim_Status) recorded as a numbered decision rather than an omission (EV8).

§5 Design / architecture

(The architectural diagram — 10-architecture-diagram-light.png, recommended — is the centrepiece of this section and is embedded here at assemble time.)

The pipeline is organised as acquisition → ingestion → validation → storage → processing → output, and distinguishes what is automated from what is manual. It runs as a single Google Colab notebook (itself in the cloud) operating on a Google Cloud Storage (GCS) bucket, so Colab and GCS share one cloud boundary; Kaggle (the data source) and the local reproducibility layer sit outside it.

5.1 The three tiers and their integrity chain

  • Bronze (ingest) — the raw CSV is fetched once (version-pinned, kagglehub version=1) and written untouched to {date}/bronze/healthcare_fraud.csv with a manifest.json (sha256 + shape). Write-once, never edited.
  • Silver (clean) — reads bronze, asserts the schema contract against its manifest, then runs cast → validate → impute waves (D1/D2), writing the cleaned result at close-of-silver (D17). Its manifest chains to bronze.
  • Gold (curate) — reads silver, featurises (velocity profiling D7/D14, log-then-standardise D13, month/weekend D3), and writes the model-ready matrix {date}/gold/ (D16/D18). Its manifest carries source_silver, split counts and fraud rate.

Each read is an integrity gate: the consuming tier verifies the source tier's sha256 + shape before ingesting. This produces a chained provenance proof — the gold matrix can be reconciled back to the raw bytes at every step.

5.2 Automated vs manual

  • Automated (Colab cells): bronze → silver → gold materialisation, each with manifest integrity gates — reproducible by re-running the notebook.
  • Manual / one-time: the Kaggle fetch (a bootstrap), the initial kagglehub_version pin, and console verification of each tier's objects in GCS.

5.3 The leak-free line

The design keeps learning out of storage: gold stores pre-encoding features; scaling and target/one-hot encoding are fit per-fold inside the training pipeline (D8/D16). Date handling and velocity profiling use only train-derived rules, never test information. This is the single most important guarantee the architecture provides to a downstream model.

§6 Implementation

The pipeline is fully implemented and its artifacts verified to exist and to reproduce.

6.1 Tiers materialised in cloud storage

All three tiers were built running the Colab notebook against the real dataset, and each verified in the GCS console (milestone_two bucket): {date}/bronze/, {date}/silver/, and {date}/gold/ each contain their data object(s) plus a manifest.json. This is the pipeline actually running end-to-end on the full 10,000-row dataset, not a stub.

6.2 Evidence scripts reproduce the report's numbers

Six reproducible evidence scripts (eda/evidence_pass1–6.py) run green against the raw CSV and regenerate every number in this report:

Script Checks Result
pass1 missingness (EV1), timeline (EV2), leakage (EV3), skew (EV4) EV1–EV4 reproduced
pass2 protected-attr signal (EV5 → D12) plots
pass3 amount transform skew (EV6 → D13) plots
pass4 imputation replication (EV7 → D1/D2) VERDICT
pass5 gold contract (EV8): 17 of 17 assertions GOLD CONTRACT 17/17
pass6 cardinality/folds/seasonality (EV9 → D4/D6/D3) 14 of 14

All scripts use a single --csv argument defaulting to the bundled dataset, so they run from the repository with no machine-specific paths.

6.3 Gold contract — the milestone deliverable

The gold output is verified to satisfy the full contract (17/17, EV8): shape (10000, 21) = 19 features + Is_Fraud + split; splits 8000 / 1000 / 1000; fraud balanced 0.0829 / 0.0830 / 0.0830; 100% of fraud ≤ 6d; Claim_Amount skew reduced 2.411 → 0.102; 0 nulls; and exclusions D10/D12/D3/identifiers all absent from the feature set.

6.4 Reproducibility of the artifact

The gold object is byte-identical on cold re-run in our environment — the sha256 digest (4541d519…) reproduces exactly. We additionally verified numeric stability across the two Python environments we tested (a clean project venv vs. the curated pinned dependencies on Python 3.12), which produced identical numbers and the same digest. Reproducibility therefore holds under the pinned requirements.txt we ship (§7) — install those exact versions and you reproduce our artifact. We do not assert byte-identical output under unpinned or untested dependency versions; the guarantee is scoped to the shipped pin-set.

§7 Reproducibility, repository & documentation

7.1 Setup and run for another student

  1. git clone <M2 repository> (public).
  2. pip install -r requirements.txt (curated, pinned, direct-deps).
  3. python eda/evidence_pass1.py … evidence_pass6.py — each runs from the bundled data/healthcare_fraud_detection.csv (no --csv needed; override provided for any other copy).

To reproduce the full bronze → silver → gold pipeline rather than just the evidence, run notebooks/Milestone_Two.ipynb in Google Colab. No hidden environment, no machine-specific paths, and no Kaggle login required to reproduce the evidence (the bundled CSV is the default; the version-pinned Kaggle fetch is documented as the acquisition path).

Running Milestone_Two.ipynb end-to-end additionally requires runtime credentials — see §7.4.

7.3 Dependencies & environment

requirements.txt lists the curated direct dependencies (data handling: pandas, numpy, pyarrow, matplotlib, seaborn, scikit-learn, category_encoders, xgboost for the downstream plan, plus acquisition/utility deps). The scripts' numeric output was verified stable across the pinned environment.

7.4 Secrets & safety

Secrets & authentication. Running the full notebook requires two external credentials, and both are handled without committing secrets to the repository — the .gitignore excludes key material, and no credential value appears in the notebook code or this repo.

  • Kaggle API key — used at the one-time dataset acquisition stage (kagglehub.dataset_download). The key is supplied via the Colab secrets manager at runtime, never hard-coded. A reviewer who only wants to reproduce the evidence does not need it: the bundled dataset in data/ is the default input to the EDA scripts (§7.1).
  • Google Cloud authentication — the notebook authenticates against the target project and reads/writes the milestone_two bucket via Colab's user-interactive auth.authenticate_user() OAuth flow. This is a runtime grant, not a stored secret: the connecting reviewer grants storage access from their own account with their own bucket permissions.

No credential value is committed to the repository.

§8 Next-step plan (Milestone 3)

8.1 Baseline model and evaluation

The gold tier is explicitly designed to feed a classifier. Milestone 3 proposes: train an XGBoost model (per the module roadmap) on the gold feature matrix, using leak-free cross-validation — StratifiedKFold in the ~8.3% fraud band, with target/one-hot encoding and scaling fit per-fold on training folds only (D8/D16). Given the class imbalance, metrics will centre on precision, recall, F1 and ROC-AUC against the 8.29% majority baseline — not accuracy.

8.2 Governance of any deployed system

Any model downstream of this pipeline is scoped to flag claims for human review, never to auto-deny (§2.3). The velocity feature, though strong, overlaps ~18% of legitimate claims and must remain a model-fed input, not a standalone rule (D14).

8.3 Honest limitations carried forward

  • Synthetic-data generalisation — a model trained on this synthetic data must be (re)validated on genuine claim data before near-deployment (§2.4).
  • Class imbalance — the stratified split preserves the rate (D6), and explicitly addressing it in the training/evaluation procedure (e.g. class-weighted loss, resampling, threshold selection) is scoped to Milestone 3, where the model itself is built.
  • Transform impact — log1p/scaling fixes are distributional hygiene, documented as such rather than claimed accuracy wins (D13).

8.4 What M3 would add

Training + evaluation from gold with provenance intact (pre-encoding storage preserved so every model input can be traced to raw bytes); a Random Forest comparison; and revalidation on real data. The pipeline's chained manifests make each of these additions a transparent, reproducible extension of this milestone's work.

D# = numbered decision-log ID (D1–D18), each earned by an EDA evidence check (EV1–EV9). These markers are used consistently in the diagram, this report, and the decision log to make every design choice traceable to the analysis that earns it.
